top10.introHtml:
Ranked by value per dollar — condition and rarity weighted over mileage. All seat 4+, under $15k, within 35 miles of Media PA.

Refreshed 2026-10-30 · 77 listings screened across Cars.com, CarGurus and AutoTrader.

picks.whyGood: Only 34k miles on a 17-year-old BMW is exceptional — likely a pampered second car. The E93 328i delivers rear-wheel-drive fun and a proper convertible experience.
picks.whatToVerify: BMW E93 cooling system (water pump, thermostat, radiator hoses), convertible hydraulic top operation, and rust on subframe/sills. Get a PPI.
picks.bottomLine: The standout of the list on mileage alone. If it passes inspection, nothing here beats it at this price.

picks.whyGood: The E46 330Ci is one of the most celebrated BMWs ever built — balanced chassis, communicative steering, silky inline-6. Under $10k for 64k miles is a genuine steal.
picks.whatToVerify: E46 cooling system failures are notorious (expansion tank, water pump, thermostat housing). Subframe cracks from PA potholes are also a concern.
picks.bottomLine: A steal if the cooling system has been addressed. Do not skip the PPI — this is the car's only real weakness.

picks.whyGood: The N54 twin-turbo inline-6 makes 300hp stock and is deeply tunable. 48k miles is excellent for a 16-year-old performance car.
picks.whatToVerify: Verify the N54 HPFP recall was completed. Check for wastegate rattle, charge pipe cracks, and valve cover gasket seepage.
picks.bottomLine: A lot of car for under $12k. The HPFP recall verification is non-negotiable — call a dealer with the VIN before buying.

picks.whyGood: 302hp V8 Mercedes convertible for under $8k is absurd value. The CLK 500 is smooth, fast, and elegant — a proper grand tourer.
picks.whatToVerify: Inspect the convertible top mechanism carefully — hydraulic failures are costly. Check ABC suspension components and look for rust underneath.
picks.bottomLine: Best V8 bang-for-buck on the entire list. Inspect hydraulic components and top mechanism before committing.

picks.whyGood: The W207 E350 Cabriolet is a luxury grand touring machine with 302hp V6 and a gorgeous profile. Rated Great Deal — and it is.
picks.whatToVerify: Inspect the soft top fabric for tears or leaks. Verify hydraulic top operation through all cycles. Check for rust on sills.
picks.bottomLine: Most recommended for comfort-over-sport. Great Deal rating at $13,888 makes this the easiest recommendation on the list.

picks.whyGood: The B8 A5 Cabriolet is one of the best-looking convertibles ever made. True 4-seat, 2.0T quattro, iconic styling that still turns heads.
picks.whatToVerify: TFSI oil consumption is common on B8 — check the dipstick before purchase. Inspect soft top fabric for wear at the rear window.
picks.bottomLine: A beautiful car at a fair price. Oil consumption check and top inspection are the two must-dos.

picks.whyGood: 50k miles on a 2007 CLK 350 is exceptional — almost certainly a pampered second car. The 272hp V6 is smooth and trouble-free.
picks.whatToVerify: Inspect convertible top through all cycles — windows, latches, hydraulics. Check for rust underneath from PA winters.
picks.bottomLine: Outstanding value on mileage. If the top is in good shape, it's worth every penny of $13k.

picks.whyGood: The G37 Convertible is underrated — 330hp naturally-aspirated V6, rear-wheel drive, proper hardtop that stows in the trunk. Rated Great Deal.
picks.whatToVerify: Hardtop retractable mechanism must work without hesitation. At 91k miles check timing chain tensioners (known VQ37 issue). Test trunk operation with top stowed.
picks.bottomLine: Great Deal badge plus RWD sporty DNA. The hardtop mechanism is the one must-inspect item.

picks.whyGood: Newest car on the list — 2016 means modern safety features, infotainment, and a proven 2.0T engine. Best modern tech of the bunch.
picks.whatToVerify: Verify DSG/S tronic mechatronic service history. Inspect soft top fabric. Check for TFSI carbon buildup on intake valves.
picks.bottomLine: Best choice for someone who wants modern connectivity and driver aids. Newest car with the fewest unknowns.

picks.whyGood: 333hp supercharged V6, quattro AWD, B8 S5 styling — a genuine performance car under $11k. A bargain in any market.
picks.whatToVerify: The supercharger coupler on the 3.0 TFSI is a known failure point — costs $500+ and must be inspected. Timing chain service may be due at 92k miles.
picks.bottomLine: Performance bargain of the entire list. Supercharger coupler inspection is non-negotiable before purchase.

manual10.introHtml: Manual-transmission convertibles from this refresh. Transmission data isn't consistently reported across sources — this section updates as stick-shift listings are confirmed.

mustangs.introHtml: All 2005+ Ford Mustang convertibles in budget. S197 and S550 generation — true rear-wheel-drive fun with the cheapest parts of any car on this list.

picks.whyGood: Sub-$10k Mustang convertible. The S197 is well-proven and parts are the cheapest on this list.
picks.whatToVerify: At 121k miles check rear axle seals, steering rack play, and convertible top condition. Verify which engine (V6 or V8 GT).
picks.bottomLine: Budget entry point. Parts cost makes this the easiest to own long-term.

picks.whyGood: Another S197 Mustang — 128k miles but Mustangs are robust. Available at a fair price.
picks.whatToVerify: 128k miles: check rear sway bar end links, control arm bushings, and spring sag. Inspect top fabric carefully for tears.
picks.bottomLine: Lowest-priced Mustang here if the $9,442 one is gone. Mustangs earn their miles.

picks.whyGood: V6 Premium trim — full features and 305hp. Lowest mileage of the three Mustangs at 97k.
picks.whatToVerify: Check for the Pony Package suspension if equipped. Verify top seals — PA rain finds any weakness. Check frame rails for rust.
picks.bottomLine: Best value of the three Mustangs: lowest mileage, proper Premium trim.

picks.whyGood: The GT badge means the 4.6L V8 — proper muscle-car convertible. Only 9 miles away in West Chester.
picks.whatToVerify: High miles on a V8 Mustang: check rear main seal, timing chain guide wear, and exhaust manifold cracks. Inspect top carefully.
picks.bottomLine: V8 power at a reasonable price. Close to home. The GT is the version to have.
